prediction.likelyOutcome: Hong is more likely than not to succeed in showing the three-day notice violated CCP § 1161(2)'s one-year limitation, since the underlying debt indisputably arose in January-February 2023 and Universal's application-of-payments theory is a legally aggressive attempt to bootstrap stale debt into a current forfeiture ground that courts are likely to reject given the anti-forfeiture policy behind UD notice requirements and Universal's own 23-month acceptance of full rent without objection. Universal likely loses possession, holdover damages, and fees in this action, though it retains a good chance of recovering the underlying $65,989 rent debt in a separate, non-UD proceeding.

issues.label: Three-Day Notice Validity / Possession Under CCP § 1161(2)
Waiver/Estoppel by Continued Acceptance of Rent

outcome.description: After a three-day court trial the trial court entered judgment for the landlord on July 3, 2025 awarding possession, $65,989 in past-due rent (the amount demanded in the notice) and $123,111 in holdover damages, $189,100 in total; no fee award is stated in the opinion. The Court of Appeal reversed, holding the three-day notice void because the unpaid rent fell due more than one year before service, and remanded for entry of judgment in favor of the tenant.
